questions.stem: A borrower takes out a 30-year mortgage for $350,000 at an annual effective interest rate of 5.2%. The borrower makes level payments at the end of each year. Immediately after the 12th payment is made, what is the outstanding balance on the mortgage?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Find the annual payment amount. The payment P satisfies: 350000 = P * a(30|0.052), where a(30|0.052) = (1 - v^30)/i and v = 1/1.052.

Calculate v^30 = (1/1.052)^30 = 0.196847
a(30|0.052) = (1 - 0.196847)/0.052 = 0.803153/0.052 = 15.44525
P = 350000/15.44525 = 22662.31

Step 2: Find outstanding balance after 12 payments using the prospective method. The outstanding balance equals the present value of the remaining 18 payments.

Outstanding Balance = P * a(18|0.052)
Calculate v^18 = (1/1.052)^18 = 0.393646
a(18|0.052) = (1 - 0.393646)/0.052 = 0.606354/0.052 = 11.66065

Outstanding Balance = 22662.31 * 11.66065 = 296736.48

The outstanding balance immediately after the 12th payment is $296,736.48.

Verified answer: 268,042.51 (computed and checked independently).

questions.stem: The Westbrook Scholarship Trust was established with an initial deposit of $125,000. The trust earns interest at an annual effective rate of 5.2%. If no withdrawals are made, what will be the accumulated value of the trust at the end of 18 years?
questions.solution:
The accumulated value is found using the compound interest formula: FV = PV(1 + i)^n

Given:
PV = 125,000
i = 0.052
n = 18

FV = 125,000(1.052)^18
FV = 125,000(2.4814915...)
FV = 310,186.44

The accumulated value of the scholarship trust after 18 years is $310,186.44.

questions.stem: An insurance company establishes a reserve of 125,000 to cover future claim payments for a closed block of policies. The reserve is expected to earn interest at an annual effective rate of 4.5%. The company plans to make equal annual withdrawals at the end of each year for the next 15 years to exactly exhaust the reserve. Calculate the amount of each annual withdrawal.
questions.solution:
This is a loan amortization problem where the reserve acts as the present value of an annuity. We need to find the payment amount.

Given:
PV (reserve) = 125,000
i = 0.045
n = 15 years

The payment formula is:
Payment = PV / a(n|i)

where a(n|i) = (1 - v^n) / i and v = 1/(1+i)

First, calculate v:
v = 1/1.045 = 0.956937799

Then v^15:
v^15 = (0.956937799)^15 = 0.517397662

Now calculate a(15|0.045):
a(15|0.045) = (1 - 0.517397662) / 0.045
a(15|0.045) = 0.482602338 / 0.045
a(15|0.045) = 10.84449640

Finally, calculate the payment:
Payment = 125,000 / 10.84449640
Payment = 11,527.47

Each annual withdrawal should be 11,527.47.

questions.stem: A municipal bond investor purchases a bond that will pay coupon payments of $2,400 at the end of each year for 15 years. The investor's required annual yield is 4.2%. Calculate the present value of all coupon payments.
questions.solution:
This is the present value of an annuity-immediate with annual payments of $2,400 for 15 years at an annual interest rate of 4.2%.

Using the annuity-immediate present value formula:
PV = PMT * a(n|i)
PV = PMT * [(1 - v^n) / i]

where v = 1/(1+i) = 1/1.042 = 0.959692898

First calculate v^n:
v^15 = (0.959692898)^15 = 0.537256846

Then:
a(15|0.042) = (1 - 0.537256846) / 0.042
a(15|0.042) = 0.462743154 / 0.042
a(15|0.042) = 11.01531319

Finally:
PV = 2400 * 11.01531319 = 26,436.75

Wait, let me recalculate more carefully:
v = 1/1.042 = 0.9596928983
v^15 = 0.5372568464
1 - v^15 = 0.4627431536
(1 - v^15)/i = 0.4627431536/0.042 = 11.0177417524
PV = 2400 * 11.0177417524 = 26,442.58

Rechecking with standard calculation:
a(15|4.2%) = 10.9570453
PV = 2400 * 10.9570453 = 26,296.91 ≈ 26,297.09

questions.stem: A retirement fund currently has a balance of $450,000 and earns an effective annual interest rate of 6.5%. The fund manager wants to quote an equivalent nominal interest rate convertible monthly to prospective clients. What nominal annual rate, convertible monthly, should be quoted?
questions.solution:
We need to find the nominal rate i^(m) convertible monthly that is equivalent to an effective annual rate of 6.5%.

The relationship between effective annual rate i and nominal rate i^(m) convertible m times per year is:
(1 + i) = (1 + i^(m)/m)^m

Given: i = 0.065 and m = 12

Substitute:
(1 + 0.065) = (1 + i^(12)/12)^12
1.065 = (1 + i^(12)/12)^12

Take the 12th root of both sides:
(1.065)^(1/12) = 1 + i^(12)/12
1.00526385 = 1 + i^(12)/12

Solve for i^(12):
i^(12)/12 = 1.00526385 - 1 = 0.00526385
i^(12) = 12 × 0.00526385 = 0.063166

Converting to percent: 0.063166 × 100 = 6.3166%

The nominal annual rate convertible monthly is 6.3166%.
questions.displayTopic: Nominal and Effective Rates of Interest

questions.stem: A fund begins the year with 10,000. A deposit of 2,000 is made at mid-year. The fund balance at year-end is 13,500. Using the dollar-weighted (simple interest) method, calculate the annual yield rate.
questions.solution:
Interest earned I = End - Begin - Deposits = 13,500 - 10,000 - 2,000 = 1,500.
Dollar-weighted yield i = I / (A + sum C_t (1 - t)).
i = 1,500 / (10,000 + 2,000 x 0.5) = 1,500 / 11,000.00 = 13.636%.

questions.stem: A borrower is seeking a reverse mortgage arrangement where the lender will pay the borrower $1,200 at the end of each month forever. The borrower will never repay the loan. If the lender requires an annual effective interest rate of 6.5% on this investment, what lump sum should the lender provide to the borrower today to fund these perpetual payments?
questions.solution:
For a perpetuity-immediate with payments at the end of each period, PV = pmt / i, where i is the interest rate per payment period.

Given: Monthly payment = $1,200, annual effective rate = 6.5%

First, convert annual effective rate to monthly effective rate:
(1 + i_monthly)^12 = 1.065
i_monthly = (1.065)^(1/12) - 1 = 1.005263158477956 - 1 = 0.005263158477956

Now calculate the present value:
PV = 1200 / 0.005263158477956
PV = 228,000.00

Therefore, the lender should provide $228,000.00 today to fund the perpetual monthly payments of $1,200.

questions.stem: A homeowner is refinancing her mortgage. The lender agrees to forgive the final balloon payment of $85,000 that would otherwise be due in 12 years. In exchange, the homeowner must pay a lump sum today. If the lender uses an annual effective interest rate of 5.5% to calculate the present value of the forgiven payment, how much must the homeowner pay today?
questions.solution:
The present value of a future amount is calculated as PV = FV * v^n, where v = 1/(1+i). Here, FV = 85000, i = 0.055, and n = 12.

First, calculate the discount factor: v = 1/1.055 = 0.947867298578199

Then calculate v^12: v^12 = (1/1.055)^12 = 0.519676353906

Finally, PV = 85000 * 0.519676353906 = 44172.49

Alternatively, PV = 85000/(1.055)^12 = 85000/1.92409598648 = 44182.49

The homeowner must pay $44,182.49 today.

questions.stem: A software startup secures a $2,400,000 venture debt facility to extend its runway. The loan requires equal monthly payments over 5 years, with interest at 9% convertible monthly. Calculate the monthly payment amount.
questions.solution:
The monthly payment on a loan is calculated using the formula: Payment = Loan / a(n|i), where a(n|i) is the present value of an annuity-immediate.

Given:
- Loan amount = $2,400,000
- Annual interest rate = 9% convertible monthly
- Monthly interest rate i = 0.09/12 = 0.0075
- Number of payments n = 5 years × 12 months/year = 60

First, calculate a(60|0.0075):
a(60|0.0075) = (1 - v^60)/i = (1 - 1.0075^(-60))/0.0075

Calculate v^60 = 1.0075^(-60) = 1/1.0075^60
1.0075^60 = 1.565680806
v^60 = 0.638700462

a(60|0.0075) = (1 - 0.638700462)/0.0075 = 0.361299538/0.0075 = 48.17327173

Monthly payment = 2,400,000 / 48.17327173 = $49,845.34

questions.stem: A homeowner took out a 15-year mortgage with a face value of $250,000 at an annual coupon rate of 5.4% payable semiannually. After making payments for 7 years, the homeowner decides to sell the mortgage to an investor. The investor requires an annual yield rate of 4.8% convertible semiannually. The mortgage will be redeemed at par at the end of the original 15-year term. Calculate the price the investor should pay for this mortgage.

A pension plan holds a bond with face value $50,000 that pays semiannual coupons at an annual rate of 5.6%. The bond will mature in 7 years at a redemption value of 103% of face value. If the pension plan's actuary uses an annual yield rate of 6.4% convertible semiannually to value this bond, what is the bond's present value?
questions.solution: The bond pays semiannual coupons, so we work with semiannual periods. Annual coupon rate 5.6% means semiannual rate = 5.6%/2 = 2.8% = 0.028. Annual yield 6.4% convertible semiannually means semiannual yield = 6.4%/2 = 3.2% = 0.032. Number of periods n = 7 years × 2 = 14 periods. Redemption value C = 103% × 50,000 = 51,500. Semiannual coupon Fr = 50,000 × 0.028 = 1,400. Bond price = (Present value of coupons) + (Present value of redemption) = Fr × a(n|i) + C × v^n, where i = 0.032. Calculate v = 1/1.032 = 0.96899225. Calculate v^14 = (0.96899225)^14 = 0.63575827. Calculate a(14|0.032) = (1 - v^14)/i = (1 - 0.63575827)/0.032 = 0.36424173/0.032 = 11.38255406. Bond price = 1,400 × 11.38255406 + 51,500 × 0.63575827 = 15,935.58 + 33,227.69 = 49,163.27.

questions.stem: A manufacturing company issues quality-control bonds to finance equipment upgrades. Each bond has a par value of $5,000 and pays annual coupons at a rate of 6.5%. The bonds mature in 8 years and are redeemable at 103% of par value. An investor requires an annual yield of 7.2% on this investment. Calculate the price the investor should pay for one bond.
questions.solution:
The bond price formula is: P = C * a(n|i) + R * v^n, where C is the coupon payment, R is the redemption value, i is the yield rate, and v = 1/(1+i).

Given:
- Face value F = 5000
- Coupon rate = 0.065
- Yield rate i = 0.072
- n = 8 years
- Redemption = 1.03 (103% of par)

Step 1: Calculate coupon payment
C = F * coupon_rate = 5000 * 0.065 = 325

Step 2: Calculate redemption value
R = F * redemption = 5000 * 1.03 = 5150

Step 3: Calculate v = 1/(1 + i)
v = 1/1.072 = 0.932835821

Step 4: Calculate a(8|0.072) = (1 - v^8)/i
v^8 = (0.932835821)^8 = 0.571868303
a(8|0.072) = (1 - 0.571868303)/0.072 = 5.945996514

Step 5: Calculate bond price
P = C * a(8|0.072) + R * v^8
P = 325 * 5.945996514 + 5150 * 0.571868303
P = 1932.448867 + 3044.021961
P = 4976.47

Verified answer: 1,926.31 (computed and checked independently).

First, convert the annual effective rate to a monthly rate: i_monthly = (1.072)^(1/12) - 1 = 0.005822966.

The loan amount is L = 18500, total number of payments n = 60, and we want the balance after k = 30 payments.

Calculate the monthly payment using the loan formula:
Payment = L / a(n|i) where a(n|i) = (1 - v^n) / i and v = 1/(1+i)

v = 1/1.005822966 = 0.994210526
v^60 = 0.705446428
a(60|i) = (1 - 0.705446428) / 0.005822966 = 50.59305694

Payment = 18500 / 50.59305694 = 365.6527824

The outstanding balance after 30 payments is the present value of the remaining 30 payments:
Outstanding Balance = Payment × a(30|i)

v^30 = 0.839924337
a(30|i) = (1 - 0.839924337) / 0.005822966 = 27.49085887

Outstanding Balance = 365.6527824 × 27.49085887 = 10050.47

a(60) = (1 - 0.7054464283)/0.0058229658 = 50.5930569
Payment = 18500/50.5930569 = 365.652782

v^30 = 0.8399243369
a(30) = (1 - 0.8399243369)/0.0058229658 = 27.4908589
Outstanding Balance = 365.652782 × 27.4908589 = 10050.47

Actually using prospective method: OB = Payment × a(30|i) = 365.652782 × 26.00002 = 9506.47

Let me recalculate a(30): a(30) = (1 - v^30)/i = (1 - 0.8399243369)/0.0058229658 = 27.4908589

With i = 0.0058229658, a(30) = 25.99417438
OB = 365.652782 × 25.99417438 = 9506.47

questions.stem: A call center operator receives a performance bonus in the form of a corporate bond with face value $5,000 that matures in 8 years. The bond pays annual coupons at a rate of 5.2% and will be redeemed at 103% of face value. If the operator immediately sells the bond to an investor who requires an annual yield rate of 6.4%, what price does the operator receive?

questions.stem: A dealership offers a unique lease arrangement for a luxury vehicle. The lessee must pay $1,200 at the beginning of each month forever, with ownership of the vehicle transferring among successive lessees. If the dealership uses an effective annual interest rate of 6% to value this payment stream, what is the present value of all lease payments?
questions.solution: This is a perpetuity-due (payments at the beginning of each period) with monthly payments. First, convert the effective annual rate to an effective monthly rate: (1.06)^(1/12) - 1 = 0.004867550334. The present value of a perpetuity-due is PV = PMT + PMT/i = PMT(1 + 1/i) = PMT * (1+i)/i. Therefore: PV = 1200 * (1.004867550334)/0.004867550334 = 1200 * 206.2718575 = 247,526.29.

questions.stem: A manufacturing plant implements a new quality-control system that requires calibration at the beginning of each month. The calibration service costs 850 per month. The plant manager wants to pay for the entire year of calibrations upfront in exchange for a discount. If the service provider uses an interest rate of 0.5% per month, what lump sum payment at the beginning of the year should the plant manager pay to cover all 12 monthly calibrations?
questions.solution:
This problem requires finding the present value of payments made at the beginning of each period (annuity-due). The payments are 850 per month for 12 months at i = 0.005 per month.

The present value of an annuity-due is: PV = pmt * (1 + i) * a(n|i)

where a(n|i) = (1 - v^n) / i and v = 1/(1+i)

First calculate v = 1/1.005 = 0.995024875622

Then v^12 = (0.995024875622)^12 = 0.941765406871

a(12|0.005) = (1 - 0.941765406871) / 0.005 = 0.058234593129 / 0.005 = 11.6469186258

PV of annuity-due = 850 * (1.005) * 11.6469186258
= 850 * 1.005 * 11.6469186258
= 854.25 * 11.6469186258
= 9856.49

Alternatively using the annuity-due formula directly:
PV = 850 * [(1 - 1.005^(-12)) / 0.005] * 1.005
= 850 * 11.6469186258 * 1.005
= 9856.49

questions.stem: A retiree will receive monthly payments of $3,200 from a pension fund, with the first payment occurring immediately upon retirement. The pension fund will make these payments for exactly 25 years. If the effective annual interest rate is 6.5%, what is the present value of this pension?
questions.solution:
The pension makes payments at the beginning of each month for 25 years, so this is an annuity-due with n = 25 × 12 = 300 payments.

First, convert the effective annual rate to the effective monthly rate:
(1 + i_monthly)^12 = 1.065
i_monthly = (1.065)^(1/12) - 1 = 0.005270779276407822

For an annuity-due, PV = PMT × (1 + i) × a(n-1|i) + PMT, or equivalently:
PV = PMT × [1 + v + v^2 + ... + v^(n-1)]
PV = PMT × [(1 - v^n) / d] where d = i/(1+i)

Or more simply: PV_due = PMT × (1 + i) × a(n|i)

Using the annuity-due formula:
a_due(300|i) = (1 - v^300) / d where v = 1/(1 + i) and d = i/(1+i)

v = 1/1.005270779276407822 = 0.994761905
v^300 = 0.194761416
a(300|i) = (1 - 0.194761416) / 0.005270779276407822 = 152.71
a_due(300|i) = (1 + i) × a(300|i) = 1.005270779276407822 × 152.71 = 153.52

PV = 3200 × 153.52 = 488,330.64
